cases.title: One shared action preserves every hidden state
cases.scenario: Two hidden futures share one observation. A common action preserves both through every declared disturbance.
cases.oracle: For the single action, all hidden-state/disturbance successors enter the same declared next belief and every hidden terminal state passes.
cases.claim_ceiling: Finite belief-state decision semantics only; no probability, geology, hydraulic, site, rights or real-world infrastructure qualification.

cases.title: Different hidden-state preferred actions do not create a robust shared action
cases.scenario: A coastal action preserves the coast world but breaks the inland world; an inland action does the reverse. The controller cannot distinguish them yet.
cases.oracle: Each action has at least one known successor floor failure in the single shared belief; existential choice of one action cannot satisfy both hidden states.
cases.claim_ceiling: Finite belief-state decision semantics only; no probability, geology, hydraulic, site, rights or real-world infrastructure qualification.

cases.title: Different actions become admissible only after a distinguishing observation
cases.scenario: One shared wait action leads to two observable-history classes. The controller may choose different actions only in the two successor beliefs.
cases.oracle: Backward recursion first qualifies both singleton successor beliefs, then the shared initial action whose observation outcomes lead to those viable beliefs.
cases.claim_ceiling: Finite belief-state decision semantics only; no probability, geology, hydraulic, site, rights or real-world infrastructure qualification.

cases.title: Successors with the same observation are merged
cases.scenario: Two hidden states and possible disturbances produce multiple hidden successors but the same next observation history.
cases.oracle: The exact set of hidden successor IDs under the common observable-history ID must match one declared successor belief.
cases.claim_ceiling: Finite belief-state decision semantics only; no probability, geology, hydraulic, site, rights or real-world infrastructure qualification.

cases.title: Unknown authority in one hidden state yields unresolved belief
cases.scenario: An action is known to pass authority in one hidden world, but the authority status is unknown in another indistinguishable world.
cases.oracle: The action is not certified admissible for every hidden state and no other action exists.
cases.claim_ceiling: Finite belief-state decision semantics only; no probability, geology, hydraulic, site, rights or real-world infrastructure qualification.

cases.title: One hidden ecological-floor failure invalidates the belief
cases.scenario: The freight/service floor passes in both hidden worlds, but an ecological floor fails in one.
cases.oracle: All required floors are conjunctive for every hidden state in the belief.
cases.claim_ceiling: Finite belief-state decision semantics only; no probability, geology, hydraulic, site, rights or real-world infrastructure qualification.

cases.title: Missing next observation mapping is unresolved
cases.scenario: The physical successor is known but the observation history delivered to the controller is missing.
cases.oracle: Without a valid observation class the solver cannot define the information state for the next action.
cases.claim_ceiling: Finite belief-state decision semantics only; no probability, geology, hydraulic, site, rights or real-world infrastructure qualification.

cases.title: Hidden future labels cannot split an unchanged observable history
cases.scenario: Two geological model labels differ, but the measurement and observation history available at the decision time are identical.
cases.oracle: The policy API contains observable-history IDs and belief membership only; hidden future labels are not policy inputs.
cases.claim_ceiling: Finite belief-state decision semantics only; no probability, geology, hydraulic, site, rights or real-world infrastructure qualification.

cases.title: Belief expansion to a floor-failing hidden state removes viability
cases.scenario: A singleton belief is viable. Adding an observationally indistinguishable hidden state whose terminal floor fails makes the belief non-viable.
cases.oracle: One common action must preserve all members; adding a hidden member with a known mandatory floor failure removes the robust witness.
cases.claim_ceiling: Finite belief-state decision semantics only; no probability, geology, hydraulic, site, rights or real-world infrastructure qualification.

cases.title: Belief graph cap returns bounded without a partial policy
cases.scenario: The hidden-state count exceeds the configured cap before solving.
cases.oracle: The limit-aware API rejects before synthesis and returns no state or policy labels.
cases.claim_ceiling: Finite belief-state decision semantics only; no probability, geology, hydraulic, site, rights or real-world infrastructure qualification.
